title: fips_aggregate() calls gate functions outside spinlock — correct for PREEMPT_RT
description: Why it is right: crypto2dev_fips_aggregate() snapshots gate function pointers and module refs under the read lock, then releases the lock and calls the gates. wolfssl's fips_gate() emits pr_err_ratelimited() which acquires a ratelimit spinlock. Calling that while already holding provider_lock (a spinlock) would be a lock ordering violation on PREEMPT_RT kernels where spinlocks are sleeping. The pattern — snapshot refs under lock, call outside — is the correct kernel idiom. What a reviewer might incorrectly suggest: 'simplify by calling the gate functions while holding the read lock.' That change would silently introduce a lock inversion bug that only manifests on PREEMPT_RT (Ubuntu RT kernels, RHEL RT). The module_put() cleanup loop on early-return-from-failure path also correctly releases refs for all uncalled gates.
close_reason: confirmed correct: snapshotting gate function pointers under read lock then calling outside lock is required for PREEMPT_RT and prevents lock ordering violation with nested spinlocks in pr_err_ratelimited
